page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-22 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The instance provisions 22 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 11 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. Memory capacity totals 176.0 GB, yielding a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of shared L3 cache. Advanced hardware execution features include AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-assisted encryption flags like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no discrete GPUs and provides no integrated local ephemeral storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark measurements position the c3-highmem-22 primarily within the median tier for compute and memory throughput. The instance recorded a multi-core score of 12208.0 and a single-core score of 1720.0 in Geekbench, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 28716.8. Stress-ng returned 18320.55 for multi-core and 1624.18 for single-core testing. Memory bandwidth reaches 106.23 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 45.62 GB/sec for writes. The platform demonstrated strong performance in small-scale language model execution, generating 297.17 tokens per second on a 135M model, while larger 7B model execution yielded 16.8 tokens per second. Redis in-memory key-value processing achieved 24.19 million SET operations per second, and PassMark database operations reached 10605.49.

The 1:8 allocation profile makes the instance cost-efficient for memory-dense services that do not require proportional CPU scaling. Eliminating bundled local drives ensures compute billing is not inflated by unused storage, though workloads requiring sustained I/O must account for external disk attachment latency and throughput caps. Supported workloads encompass in-memory databases like Redis, medium-scale relational databases, distributed caching layers, memory-bound data transformation pipelines, and lightweight model inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-22 is a memory-oriented virtual instance configured with 22 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 176.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, backed by 105 MB of L3 cache and support for AMX and AVX-512 extensions. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external storage attachments. Benchmark evaluations show solid median-range capabilities, including 12208.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 24.19 million Redis SET operations per second, and uncached read bandwidth of 106.23 GB/sec. The instance delivers high resource density for workloads requiring large working memory without oversized core allocations, making it well matched for in-memory databases, caching services, ETL jobs, and relational database hosting.
